$comment: One record per JSONL line in docs/ALL_FEATURES.jsonl. Developer-facing feature inventory, EN-only, single source of truth about implemented functionality. Replaces dev/FUNCTIONALITY.log; chronology comes from git history + release diffs. Public showcase lives in docs/FEATURES*.md.
title: ALL_FEATURES record

id.$comment: Stable identifier, kebab '<area>.<feature>'. It also fixes the record boundary, and S1933 draws that boundary by the gate answer rather than by the screen: a capability whose halves give different answers to 'which BuildConfig flag is this behind' is two records, because 'gate' is single-valued and validate.ps1 equates 'flavors' with that flag's row - one record spanning both answers can only lie in one of two directions. Splitting such a record keeps the old id for neither half: in both known cases the id named the very half being carved off, so a 'surviving' id would put the wrong boundary straight back into the name. The split is done when a record is next touched, not as a sweep - a spanning record only causes harm at the moment someone gives it a gate, and validate.ps1 already refuses that pairing.

area.$comment: Functional area of the capability, from a CLOSED list. S2842 closed it: the field had been a free string and had accumulated 91 distinct values across 1059 records, among them near-duplicates differing only in case and spelling ('Wear' / 'wear-os' / 'Wear OS' / 'Wear OS UI'), so any count of 'how many capabilities do we have in area X' split into twin groups and needed hand-merging before it could be read. The enum below is the vocabulary, and it is the ONLY one: scripts/quality/assert-allfeatures-sync.ps1 reads this array and refuses a record whose area is not in it, which is also why nothing else in the repository restates the list - a restated grid goes stale silently (S1392). The list was derived by grouping the values already in use rather than invented, so every entry is either a value with a double-digit record count or the centre of a group of near-duplicates. Widening it is a one-line edit HERE and nowhere else, and it is the right move when a genuinely new subject arrives; folding a new capability into 'General' to avoid the edit is what produced the 91 values in the first place. Narrowing it is not: two areas merge only by migrating the records that carry them, because a value left in the ledger with no enum entry fails the gate for whoever runs it next. 'Media Player' is deliberately not a duplicate of 'Video Player' and 'Audio Player' - it holds the records that do not state which medium they are about, and splitting them would mean judging each record's text, which the S2842 migration explicitly did not do.

name.$comment: Short EN title of the capability.

description.$comment: EN description of what the capability does.

flavors.$comment: Build variants where the capability is available. S1934 fixes how the set is derived: from the build system, never from the build the change happened to be tested on - the flag's row in docs/FLAVOR_MATRIX.md when the capability sits behind a gate, and the full set when nothing gates it, because a capability nothing narrows cannot be narrower than the app. A set that is neither the full set nor equal to some flag's row claims a reach the build system does not produce; validate.ps1 counts those against a ratchet baseline rather than refusing each one, since 242 records predate the rule. A capability living entirely in the wear module carries the full set: the watch app is its own installation and no phone build excludes it, so any narrower set here asserts a PHONE exclusion the build does not have. A watch capability that does need the phone bridge is gated by SUPPORT_WEAR_COMPANION instead. Since S2090 the wear module has a flavor dimension of its own, and a capability present in only one of ITS variants says so in 'wearFlavors' - this field stays about the phone either way.

gate.$comment: S1929. The BuildConfig flag this capability lives behind, e.g. 'SUPPORT_WEAR_COMPANION'. OPTIONAL, and its absence is an assertion rather than an omission: it means the capability is behind no flag at all, which is why documentation-only and watch-standalone records carry no gate and keep their own flavor sets. When present, scripts/all_features/validate.ps1 requires 'flavors' to equal that flag's row in docs/FLAVOR_MATRIX.md exactly, and a flag the matrix does not list is an error rather than a skip - a typo must not silently switch the check off. S1982 admits one shape beyond a single name: flags joined by '+' are a CONJUNCTION, meaning the capability needs every named flag at once, and 'flavors' must then equal the intersection of their rows exactly. Live-stream casting is the shape it exists for - the stream comes from SUPPORT_STREAMS, the receiver from SUPPORT_CAST, and neither row alone is true of it. This is still not a list of alternatives: no syntax here ever means 'any of these flags', because a capability sitting behind two different answers is two capabilities, or a record boundary drawn in the wrong place (S1933). Term order is the author's and is not normalised; a repeated term is an error, since it narrows nothing and only hides a mistyped second flag.

wearFlavors.$comment: S2090. Which WEAR-MODULE build variants the capability exists in. OPTIONAL, and absence is an assertion: it means every watch build has it, which is why naming both variants is refused rather than accepted as a synonym. This is a separate axis from 'flavors', not a reinterpretation of it: 'flavors' names PHONE variants and answers 'which phone build gates this companion capability', and the S1934 ratchet only counts a set as explained when it equals the full set or some flag's row. A capability living only in the watch's noLegal build is gated by no phone flavor at all, so under 'flavors' alone it would be forced to claim the full set and thereby assert availability everywhere - which is the one thing it must not say. Redefining 'flavors' for watch records instead was rejected: S1951 changed one flag's row and thirty records stopped matching it in a single step, twenty about the watch and ten not, so a silent change of meaning across live records is a known failure mode here.

spec.$comment: Provenance: source spec ticket id, or null when not spec-tracked.

status.$comment: Lifecycle state of the record. Defaults to 'active'.
